newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's young OTC market rises to record.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's young OTC market rises to record.

text.p: Taiwan's fledgling over-the-counter securities exchange has risen to three consecutive record highs, spurred by two major state funds being permitted to invest substantially in stocks.
The OTC index on Wednesday ended up 4.75 points, or 2.53 percent, to 192.46, the exchange said in a statement.
The rise appeared unconnected to the U.S. election victory of incumbent President Bill Clinton, which was cited as a factor in strong showings on Wednesday in other Asian stock markets.
Rather, the bull run reflected recent financial reforms that will benefit the main Taiwan Stock Exchange and the young OTC market.
Taipei announced last week it would allow the T$188 billion labour insurance fund and T$24 billion employee pension fund to invest up to 30 percent of their values in stocks.
The labour insurance fund had been barred from investing in stocks while the pension fund was limited to just 10 percent.
The OTC exchange's daily turnover has been surging since it inaugurated a new trading system in September 1995.
Before that the daily average had been in the T$1-2 million range. On Wednesday, the turnover was a robust T$5.298 billion, although that was lower than peak levels in May.
The new system requires securities brokerages to pay only deposits to the OTC exchange before trading, rather than having to pay for stocks in full at the time of purchase.
There are 69 firms listed in the OTC exchange, which has said it hopes to reach 100 listings by end-1996.
